text: Anticipatory grief (AG) refers to the experience of grief symptoms by patients or their caregivers in response to life-threatening illnesses, even before an actual loss has occurred. The selection of valid and reliable patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) to assess AG is essential for early identification, effective intervention, and the reduction of prolonged grief disorder. This study summarizes psychometric properties of AG PROMs and recommends the most effective PROMs.
source_label: Patient-reported outcome measures for anticipatory grief: a systematic review
